correctness.rationale: The source layer functional and dimension theorem determine the full affine hull. Centering the layer vector gives the exact orthogonal projection of the ambient origin, and every root vector has norm squared 2 and layer increment 1, yielding the common radius exactly. A self-contained finite-point lemma proves that a common vertex sphere is the unique minimum enclosing sphere exactly when its center lies in the convex hull; strict separation gives a strictly smaller sphere otherwise. Convex-hull membership is exactly a nonnegative edge-flow equation. In the standard bipartite orientation, max-flow/min-cut reduces this to the proportional Hall inequalities.

value.rationale: Semi-balanced root polytopes are a canonical recent graph-polytope family whose literature emphasizes lattice, Ehrhart, and spanning-tree structure. The theorem exposes a realization-sensitive Euclidean structure that is invisible to those invariants: every member has a canonical all-vertex sphere, and a sharp flow condition decides whether that sphere is actually optimal. For standard bipartite orientations, the result turns a Euclidean minimum-enclosing-ball question into the natural proportional Hall expansion criterion, with every connected biregular graph as an immediate exact-radius family.
